content.text:
# Training Task Protocol

How this mod grades a player against the training dummy's random slot playback,
and how an external application defines the tasks and reads the results.

Same channel constraint as the other protocols: REFramework's Lua has no
sockets and no HTTP server, so **the filesystem is the only channel**, and
everything below is a contract — change one side and the other breaks, usually
silently.

All paths are relative to `reframework/data/` and are declared in one place,
[`autorun/fgcnote/func/Task/Paths.lua`](autorun/fgcnote/func/Task/Paths.lua).

This file is the app↔mod contract. How the mod-side *implementation* is split
across modules is [`func/Task/README.md`](autorun/fgcnote/func/Task/README.md).

> Sibling feature: recording exchange is [`PROTOCOL.md`](PROTOCOL.md). This
> feature shares the slot **witness** format (PROTOCOL.md, *Slot names*) and the
> canonical character names (PROTOCOL.md §5) with it, and nothing else. Each
> has its own bridge folder and its own id sequence.

---

## 0. The model

The player records dummy behaviours into the 8 recording slots and enables the
game's own random playback. Every playback is one **trial**:

```
IsReplayNow:  false ──────┐ rising edge          falling edge ┌────── false
                          └──── true (slot N playing) ────────┘
                          │                                   │
                     trial opens                        settle starts
                     slot latched                       trial resolves once
                     witness checked                    outcome is decided
```

**`IsReplayNow` does not fall between two consecutive slots.** SF6's
random-slot playback chains recordings back to back with no neutral gap
(confirmed live 2026-08-04) — the boolean can stay `true` all the way through
a switch from slot N to slot M, with only the underlying `SlotID` changing
under it. Worse, when the random pick repeats the same slot twice in a row,
**`SlotID` does not change either** — nothing in `{IsReplayNow, SlotID}` alone
distinguishes "still playing" from "started over".

A trial boundary is therefore any of: `IsReplayNow`'s rising/falling edge,
`SlotID` changing while it stays `true`, or (for the same-slot repeat)
`app.TrainingInput.RecordData[1].Cursor` resetting while it stays `true` —
`Cursor` is the dummy's frame position within its own current playback, so it
drops back to (near) zero every time a playback restarts, same slot or not.
Whichever fires, the next trial opens on the same frame the previous one
closes, using that frame for the new trial and the previous frame for the one
being closed. Relying on `IsReplayNow`/`SlotID` alone would silently glue two
trials' contacts into one record and grade it against the first slot's rules.

> `Cursor` is read via `GameState.replay_cursor`
> ([`infra/GameState.lua`](autorun/fgcnote/infra/GameState.lua)). Verified live
> 2026-08-04 via `fgcnote/devtools/watch/playback.json`: `RecordData` is a 2-element
> array indexed by **side** (0 = 1P, 1 = 2P), not by `SlotID` — confirmed by
> moving the dummy from 2P to 1P and watching the live values move from index
> 1 to index 0. Since the dummy is always P2 by this suite's convention
> (PROTOCOL.md), `RecordData[1]` is always its live playback record, no
> `SlotID`-based indexing involved. What is still unconfirmed is only the
> *reset-on-restart* behavior this whole mechanism leans on (does `Cursor`
> reliably drop to 0 on every new play, including a same-slot repeat) — the
> live values read correctly, but that specific transition has not yet been
> watched happen. It is deliberately an *additional* boundary source, not a
> replacement for `SlotID`: if it never fires, trials still open/close
> correctly on every `IsReplayNow` edge and every `SlotID` change, same as
> before it existed — only the same-slot-repeat case silently degrades back to
> being merged, exactly as it would without it.

The mod observes what happened inside that window — every contact on either
side, latched at the frame it occurred — and on the trial's close writes one
**observation record**. Grading is a lookup into app-authored rules.

**The mod classifies; the app scores.** The points the mod reports are computed
from a table the app itself sent down, so the mod can draw live feedback — but
they are a derived convenience, and the observation record is the authority.

> **The app persists the verdicts it showed, not the observations.** Since
> 2026-09-02 the app stores one compact result per session — per-trial verdict
> and points as graded at the time — and drops contacts, action ids and the
> full spec at its staging boundary (`fgcNote/SYSTEM-BOUNDARIES.md`). A later
> rule or weight change applies to future sessions only; nothing re-grades
> history. The observation record still travels on this wire so the app can
> grade live and show breakdowns; it is transport, not a durable archive.

### Recording end is not outcome end

`IsReplayNow` is a pure function of the recording's frame count: it goes false
when the recorded inputs run out, not when the dummy's animation ends. Since
2026-08-29 that edge starts the slotResponse **settle phase** instead of closing
the trial: SmartPlayback holds the next slot, and Task keeps observing until
the dummy's `act_st` says the outcome is decided (§4, using the same predicate
as reversalResponse in §6).

Authors therefore do **not** have to pad a throw, attack or movement recording
with trailing neutral frames. The recording contains the behaviour; recovery
and the player's punish remain in the observation window even after its inputs
run out. There is deliberately no author-controlled timeout. A bounded window
that never reaches a decided state, or one displaced by an unexpected slot
hand-off, is recorded with `trial_truncated` and not scored (§4).

Verified live 2026-08-29 with a 93-frame Ryu forward-throw recording: two
trials both stayed open for 143 frames, retained `dummyCaught=true`, and carried
no diagnostic. Procedure and exact bridge evidence:
[`docs/records/2026-08-29-slot-response-settle.md`](../docs/records/2026-08-29-slot-response-settle.md).

---

## 1. Command bridge

`fgcnote/task/command.json` → `fgcnote/task/result.json`, polled at
2 Hz backing off to 0.2 Hz — the same machinery, id idempotency and reload
recovery as the other bridges (PROTOCOL.md §2 explains the rules; derive the
next id from the higher of the two files' ids).

| `action` | Effect | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| `startSession` | Validates the spec, arms the trial watcher | Sync |
| `stopSession` | Ends the running session, publishes final state | Sync |
| `listReversals` | Reads the dummy's live reversal config, for authoring (§6) | Sync |

`listReversals` answers into `result.json` alongside the usual fields:

```jsonc
{ "id": 22, "ok": true, "message": "reversals read", "appliedAt": "…",
  "characterName": "Ken", "slotsPerGroup": 10,
  "reversals": {
    "down":   [ { "slot": 1, "fields": { "IsActive": true, "Type": 2, … },
                  "active": true, "type": 2, "skillIndex": 5, … }, … ],
    "guard":  [ … ], "damage": [ … ] } }
```

`fields` is the authoritative raw scalar-field map captured from the live
reversal entry; the named keys beside it are a display projection. It is a
**read on the command bridge, not a published
mirror** — `recording_slots.json` belongs to the recording feature, and nothing watches
reversals continuously; they are read once while a task is authored.

```jsonc
// command.json                            // result.json
{ "id": 21,                                { "id": 21,
  "action": "startSession",                  "ok": true,
  "spec": { ... }  /* §2 */ }                "message": "session started: 20 trials",
                                             "taskId": "poke-defense-drill",
                                             "appliedAt": "2026-08-04T09:12:33Z" }
```

### `startSession` is refused, with a reason, when

| Condition | Message |
|---|---|
| Not in training mode | `not in training mode` |
| No dummy detected | `no dummy character detected` |
| Dummy is a different fighter | `spec is for X but the dummy is Y` |
| A session is already running | `a session is already running` |
| A `slotResponse` starts while SmartPlayback's app or in-game switch is off, or SmartPlayback failed to load | `SmartPlayback must be enabled for slot-response tasks` |
| Spec fails validation (§2) | names the first failing field |

The same prerequisite is watched for the whole run. If either SmartPlayback
switch turns off, the session stops with `SmartPlayback disabled during
session`; it never falls back to recording-edge grading.

`stopSession` with nothing running answers `no session running`. Stopping is
also forced from the mod's side when training mode is left mid-session or the
script reloads; the session document says which (§3).

---

## 2. The task spec

Sent inline in `startSession`. The mod holds it in memory for the session and
never writes it anywhere.

```jsonc
{
    "schema": 1,
    "taskId": "poke-defense-drill",      // opaque to the mod, echoed everywhere
    "type": "slotResponse",              // or "reversalResponse" -- §6
    "trialCount": 20,                    // session ends when this many resolve
    "characterName": "Ken",              // canonical name (PROTOCOL.md §5) of the
                                         // dummy this spec was authored against
    "slots": [
        {
            "id": 3,                     // 1-8, app numbering, as everywhere else
            "label": "poke 2MK",         // echoed into trial records, for humans
            "witness": {                 // exactly PROTOCOL.md's slot-name witness:
                "frames": 214,           // the recording this spec describes
                "samples": "5|6|6|2MK|5|5|5|5"
            },
            "rules": [
                { "when": "punish",  "points": 2 },
                { "when": "block",   "points": 1 },
                { "when": "got_hit", "points": -1 },
                { "when": "else",    "points": 0 }
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

### Rules: first match wins

Rules are evaluated **in the order written; the first match ends the lookup.**
That ordering is how compound truths resolve: a punish counter may plausibly
also raise the plain-counter flag, so an app that scores them differently puts
`punish` before `counter` — the mod imposes no precedence of its own.

| `when` | Matches a trial where |
|---|---|
| `damage` | any player attack contacted the dummy as a hit |
| `counter` | a contact on the dummy carried the counter flag |
| `punish` | a contact on the dummy carried the punish-counter flag |
| `block` | the player blocked a dummy attack — read off the player's guard state, §5 |
| `got_hit` | the player was hit by a dummy attack |
| `thrown` | the player was thrown — read off act_st, not dmg_attr; see §3's note on `dummyCaught` |
| `action` | the player performed one of `actionIds` (required field, ids as in the observation record) |
| `else` | always — put it last as the explicit "nothing above" score |

### Ignored slots — declaring the filler

A drill's random rotation usually has to hold behaviour that is not the drill:
a walk forward, a neutral pause, something so the dummy is not a metronome.
Those plays are trials as far as the game is concerned, and grading them makes
no sense. A slot entry can say so:

```jsonc
{ "id": 5, "label": "walk back and forth", "ignore": true,
  "witness": { "frames": 96, "samples": "5|6|4|5|5|5|5|5" } }
```

Such a play resolves into **nothing**: no observation record, no trial number,
nothing toward `trialCount`, no effect on `totalPoints`. It is counted, in the
session document's `ignored` (§3), so a user can see how much of what they are
watching is scenery.

One practical consequence: filler skips §0's settle phase. Nothing is graded,
so nothing has to be decidable after the recording ends, and
`trial_truncated` cannot fire on it.

An ignored entry **still carries a witness** and **must carry no `rules`** —
the witness because everything the spec names carries proof of what it thought
was there, so re-recording over the filler degrades to `spec_mismatch` (the
witness is checked first, and outranks `ignore`) instead of being skipped
forever in silence; no rules because rules on something never graded is a
contradiction, not a preference. A spec in which *every* entry is ignored is
refused: it would arm a session whose trial counter never moves.

**`ignore` must be declared; it is never inferred from absence.** A rule of
"a slot the spec does not mention is skipped" would be easier to author and
would delete the only signal a wrong `GAME_SLOT_BASE` ever produces — see *What
the witness check does not backstop* in §4. An unmentioned slot therefore keeps
reporting `no_spec_for_slot`, loudly, and that is the point of it.

The same field, with the same meaning and the same two rules, is legal on a
`reversals[]` entry (§6). There it also makes the trial skip the settle phase,
since an ignored trial has no answer to wait for.

**An unrecognised `when` fails the whole `startSession`**, exactly like an
unrecognised section name in `refreshState`: a typo must surface immediately,
not as a rule that quietly never matches. Same for an `action` rule without a
non-empty numeric `actionIds`, a slot `id` outside 1–8, a duplicated slot `id`,
a missing witness, a non-ignored entry without rules, an ignored entry *with*
rules, or a `trialCount` outside 1–500. Slots the spec does not mention are
legal — trials for them are recorded as `no_spec_for_slot` (§4).

---

## 3. The session stream

One file, `fgcnote/task/session.json`, **rewritten atomically in full**
on session start, on every resolved trial, and on session end. No separate
event log: the file is the whole session, oldest trial first.

```jsonc
{
    "schema": 1,
    "sequence": 12,                      // strictly increasing per write;
                                         // survives script reloads
    "taskId": "poke-defense-drill",
    "sessionState": "running",           // "running" | "finished" | "stopped"
    "stopReason": null,                  // set when "stopped": "stopped by app",
                                         // "left training mode", "script reloaded mid-session"
    "startedAt": "2026-08-04T09:12:40Z",
    "trialTarget": 20,
    "trialsDone": 3,
    "discarded": 0,                      // trials voided by the pause menu (§4)
    "ignored": 2,                        // plays of a slot the spec marked
                                         //   `ignore` — counted, never recorded (§2)
    "totalPoints": 4,                    // derived; see §0's warning
    "trials": [ /* observation records, below */ ]
}
```

### The observation record

```jsonc
{
    "trial": 3,
    "slotId": 3,                         // 1-8, app numbering
    "label": "poke 2MK",                 // echoed from the spec; null if no spec
    "diagnostic": null,                  // null | "no_spec_for_slot"
                                         //      | "spec_mismatch" | "trial_truncated"
    "frames": 214,                       // trial open to trial close (§4)
    "playerReceived": [                  // dummy's attacks reaching the player
        { "f": 88, "attr": 1036, "guardSt": 32787, "counter": false, "punish": false }
    ],
    "dummyReceived": [                   // player's attacks reaching the dummy
        { "f": 130, "attr": 33, "guardSt": 32768, "counter": false, "punish": true }
    ],
    "playerActionIds": [ 700, 810 ],     // distinct, first-seen order, max 32
    "dummyActionIds": [ 331, 341 ],      // same, for the dummy
    "playerCaught": false,               // player's act_st visited CATCH (37)
    "dummyCaught": false,                // same, for the dummy
    "matchedRule": 1,                    // 1-based index into the slot's rules;
    "points": 2                          //   both null when diagnostic is set
}
```

- `f` is frames **since the trial opened**, not a global counter.
- One entry per contact. A contact opens when the receiver's damage attribute
  goes nonzero and closes when it returns to zero; **flags are OR-ed across the
  contact's lifetime**, so a flag the game raises a frame late is still caught.
  Consecutive hits with no clean frame between them merge into one entry.
- `attr` is a `DMG_ATTR` flag mask and `guardSt` a `GUARD_ST` flag mask — §5.
- Contacts are read off the **receiving** player. That is where the game keeps
  them: whether *this* player was counter-hit, and what guard state *this*
  player was in.
- **A throw never opens a contact.** Confirmed live 2026-08-05: three
  zero-defense throw trials all closed with `playerReceived` completely empty
  — dmg_attr stays zero the whole way through a grab, so `damage`/`counter`/
  `punish`/`block`/`got_hit` are all structurally blind to it. `playerCaught`
  /`dummyCaught` are a separate latch, read off `act_st` (nBattle.ACT_ST.ID
  37 = CATCH) instead of `attr`.
- **CATCH belongs to the thrower, not the receiver.** Same three trials:
  the dummy threw the player and every one came back `dummyCaught: true`,
  `playerCaught: false`. CATCH is the act_st of *performing* a grab, not of
  being caught by one — so "the player was thrown" is read off `dummyCaught`
  (the dummy did the catching), which is what the `thrown` rule (§2) uses.
  Symmetrically, a player-throws-dummy trial would show `playerCaught: true`.
  A later direction-controlled capture identified the receiving side as
  **HOLD(38)** on the same frame the thrower entered CATCH, with `dmg_attr=0`;
  an ordinary throw then stayed HOLD for 60F before DAMAGE(32). This was
  measured in both directions on SF6 build 24176760; see
  `docs/records/2026-08-29-timeline-observation-feasibility.md`.
- **Both sides carry the same fields.** The player being counter-hit is as real
  a fact as the dummy being counter-hit, and the dummy's action ids are what a
  wakeup-option task will read the way this one reads the player's. These fields
  are transient — gone by the next frame — so the choice is between observing
  them and never being able to. Redundancy here is cheap; a frame that went
  unobserved cannot be recovered. What a given task type *uses* is decided by
  its rules, downstream.

### Reader beware

Everything in PROTOCOL.md §1's *Reader beware* applies verbatim: the file can
be briefly absent mid-rename (retry, don't error), `fs.watch` fires more than
once (dedupe on `sequence`), `sequence` going backwards means deletion, a
`schema` mismatch should be refused, and REFramework's encoder renders empty
lists as `null` — an uncontacted trial's `playerReceived` may be `null`, `[]`
or `{}`.

A `session.json` left behind by a script reload is rewritten as
`sessionState: "stopped"` the next time the mod loads — the file never claims
a session that no longer exists.

---

## 4. Trial lifecycle

```
armed ── opens ── active ── recording falls ── settling ── closes ── resolved
  │      latch SlotID  │                         │          grade, publish
  │      witness check │                         └─ dummy outcome decided
  └── replay already   ├─ pause menu: discard
      running at start:├─ filler: ignore immediately
      drain, unscored  └─ slot/cursor hand-off: close previous immediately,
                             then open the next on the same frame
```

A trial whose slot the spec marked `ignore` (§2) resolves as neither: it is
counted in `ignored` and nothing else happens. That outranks the discard —
filler was never an answer, so opening the pause menu during it does not make
it a voided one — but not the witness, which is checked first and can still
turn it into a `spec_mismatch` that is recorded and graded like any other.

"Opens" fires on `IsReplayNow`'s rising edge, on `SlotID` changing while it is
already `true`, or on `Cursor` resetting while `SlotID` stays the same (§0 —
consecutive slots chain with no gap, and a repeat of the same slot changes
neither `IsReplayNow` nor `SlotID`). A normal falling edge starts settling;
`neutral` or `restrained` closes after that frame is absorbed, while
`own_action`, `resolving`, an unclassified id or a missing sample keeps the
window open. SmartPlayback prevents the next slot from entering meanwhile.

A `SlotID`/`Cursor` hand-off still closes the previous trial on its preceding
frame because the current frame already belongs to the new recording. If it
interrupts an unresolved settle phase, the old trial is `trial_truncated`.
The settle phase has a non-authorable 900-frame safety bound; reaching it is
also `trial_truncated`, including when the final state is merely unclassified.

Diagnostics — the trial is recorded in full but `matchedRule`/`points` are
null and `totalPoints` is unaffected:

| `diagnostic` | Meaning | Decided |
|---|---|---|
| `no_spec_for_slot` | The played slot has no entry in the spec | trial opens |
| `spec_mismatch` | The live slot's witness does not match the spec's — the recording was changed after the spec was authored | trial opens |
| `trial_truncated` | The outcome was still undecided when a hand-off or the 900-frame safety bound forced the window closed | trial closes |

`spec_mismatch` is the same freshness mechanism as slot names (PROTOCOL.md,
*The witness, and why every name needs one*): slot ids are ephemeral, the game
overwrites slots freely, and a task definition that names a slot must carry
proof of what it thinks is in it. Re-record slot 3 and slot 3's trials degrade
to `spec_mismatch` — visibly — until the app republishes the spec.

The witness is re-checked every time a trial opens, not once per session
(~20 reflection calls, PROTOCOL.md's numbers).

### What the witness check does *not* backstop

The game's internal `SlotID` is 0-based against the app's 1–8 — confirmed live
2026-08-04 by watching a trial labelled slot 2 play back the recording the
game's own menu shows in slot 2.

That had to be confirmed by looking, because **the witness check cannot detect a
wrong base.** Both sides of the comparison are indexed by the same app number:
the mod converts `SlotID` to an app id, looks up *that* spec entry, and derives
the live witness from *that* live slot. An app builds its spec from the slots it
read out of `recording_slots.json`, so `spec[N].witness` and `live_witness(N)` are the same
bytes by construction, and the comparison is an identity with respect to the
base. A wrong base picks the wrong N on both sides at once and matches anyway —
mis-labelling the trial and grading it against the wrong slot's rules, silently.

What does surface a wrong base is a shifted id landing on a slot the spec does
not name: `no_spec_for_slot`, on every trial where that happens. Whether it
happens at all depends on the spec's coverage. A spec naming all eight slots
hides the shift everywhere except at the end, where a +1 shift turns the last
slot into app id 9 and there is no entry for it. A spec naming one slot out of a
rotation of two loses *every* trial, because both shifted ids miss the only entry
there is.

The narrow test, if this is ever in doubt again: put two slots in the random
rotation and name only one of them in the spec. A correct base grades that slot
and reports the other as `no_spec_for_slot`; a base off by one reports *both*
that way.

`spec_mismatch` remains what it always was — a freshness check against the slot
being re-recorded — and is unrelated to this.

---

## 5. Contact vocabulary

Dumped 2026-08-04 from the live game via `TypeDump.inspect_enum`; JSON copies in
`reframework/data/fgcnote/devtools/data/enum/`.

**Every value here is a flag mask. Test with bitwise AND, never equality** —
blocking a low arrives as `grd|lo` = 66, and `attr == 64` misses every one.

`nBattle.nHit.DMG_ATTR` (`attr` in the observation record), complete:

| Flag | Value | Meaning on a contact |
|---|---|---|
| `hi` / `lo` / `air` | 1 / 2 / 4 | the attack's hit level |
| `all` / `dis` | 8 / 16 | |
| `hit` | 32 | it landed as a hit |
| `grd` | 64 | it was blocked — **but see the warning below** |
| `armor` / `atemi` | 128 / 256 | absorbed |
| `parry` / `d_grd` | 512 / 1024 | parried / Drive-blocked |
| `hit_catch` / `resv_dmg` | 2048 / 4096 | |
| `blk_upp` / `blk_low` / `blk_air` | 8192 / 16384 / 32768 | `blocking` = all three = 57344 |

`nBattle.nHit.GUARD_ST` (`guardSt`), the groups that share the field:

| Flag | Value | |
|---|---|---|
| `GUARD_SELF` | 1 | |
| `STAND_NG` / `CROUCH_NG` | 2 / 4 | riding on the **attack**: cannot be blocked standing / crouching — which is why a spec never has to hand-label required block height |
| `GUARD_STAND` / `GUARD_CROUCH` / `GUARD_AIR` | 8 / 16 / 32 | the receiver's **actual** guard state |
| `GUARD_AUTO` | 256 | |
| `DMY_GUARD_HI/MID/LOW`, `DMY_PARRY`, `DMY_JUST` | 512…8192 | the dummy's configured guard behaviour |
| `INFO_SET` | 32768 | the field is populated — rides on every live sample |

### A blocked contact does not set `grd`

Confirmed live 2026-08-04, and it is the single most expensive thing in this
section to get wrong. Every blocked contact in the first real capture arrived as

```
attr 1036 = air|all|d_grd     grd CLEAR
guardSt 32787 = INFO_SET|GUARD_CROUCH|STAND_NG|GUARD_SELF
```

— a crouch block of a low, stated plainly by `guardSt` and not at all by the bit
named `grd`. A contact the player did *not* block came back with `guardSt`
32768, `INFO_SET` and nothing else. The first implementation tested `attr & grd`,
so it never once registered a block and every blocked trial fell silently
through to `else`.

**Decide "was this blocked" from `guardSt & (GUARD_STAND|GUARD_CROUCH|GUARD_AIR)`**
— the game says it outright — and treat the `attr` blocking bits as a widening
OR, not as the test. `func/Task/Predicate.lua`'s `is_block` is that reading, and
`tools/smoke.lua` pins it against those exact numbers.

Counter flags, on the **receiving** `cPlayer` (confirmed live 2026-08-04):
`counter_dm_flag` = Counter, `counter_fw_flag` = Punish Counter. Read on both
players, so `playerReceived[].counter` means the player was counter-hit and
`dummyReceived[].counter` means the dummy was. Whether a punish also raises
`counter_dm_flag` is unconfirmed — §2's first-match ordering is what makes the
answer not matter.

`Record.finish`'s final-frame backstop tests the dummy's `act_st` against
`nBattle.ACT_ST.ID`: `{ 13 ATCK_LAND, 29 ATCK, 30 SPECIAL, 31 SUPER, 37 CATCH,
38 HOLD }`. The slotResponse settle machine additionally marks its forced
handoff/cap paths truncated even when the numeric state is unclassified.

---

## 6. reversalResponse

The second task type in schema 1 (2026-08-05): a trial is one execution of a
configured **Reversal** — the pause menu's "when I get knocked down / block /
get hit, do this" lists — instead of one random-slot playback. The bridge
(§1), the session stream and observation record (§3), rule evaluation and the
contact vocabulary (§2's table, §5) are all unchanged; this section is only
what differs.

### The trial source

The reversal runtime lives at `TrainingManager.get_ReversalFunc()._gData`
(`app.training.tf_ReversalSetting.GameLocalData`), sampled per frame into
`GameState` ([`infra/GameState.lua`](autorun/fgcnote/infra/GameState.lua)). Its `_State`
(`EReversalState`) idles at `READY`(2), and one reversal runs:

```
READY(2) ── PLAY_WAIT(3) ── PLAYING(4) ── PLAY_END(5) ── READY(2) ─────────────
   idle      the Delay       dispatch,     HOLDS while     idle
             frames          sub-frame     the move runs
             │              │                          │                     │
             identity       trial opens   reversal ends;              dummy settles;
             latched                      settle phase starts         trial closes
```

**The trial opens at the dispatch, not at the head of the Delay** (changed
2026-08-25 — Jaes's call, all three groups alike): the window is the dummy's
*reaction*, so the configured Delay and the getup/blockstun before it are
preamble, not trial data. Two consequences, both deliberate: a reversal
**stuffed during its delay** never dispatches and files no trial, and a
reversal that rolls 不動作 never leaves `READY` and files none either — no
reaction, no reaction window.

**`PLAYING`(4) never survives to a sampled frame.** Across both 2026-08-24
capture runs the per-frame sampler saw `_State` 3 on 430 frames, 5 on 58, and
4 on **zero**, while the `Playing` handler's hook did fire — the machine runs
3 → 4 → 5 inside one frame's update. The rising edge is therefore `_State`
crossing from below `PLAYING` to `PLAYING` **or beyond**, observed in practice
as 3 → 5.

**`PLAY_END` does not mean the reversal ended.** Confirmed live 2026-08-05:
even a 20-frame forward walk spends its whole visible duration in 5 — the enum
name describes the dispatch's perspective, not the observer's. The falling
edge is the return to `READY`. Confirmed the same session: `_State` was
watched returning to `READY` between consecutive reversals, and a
RECORDING-type reversal does **not** raise `IsReplayNow`, so the two task
types cannot mistake each other's events.

**Nor does the falling edge mean the dummy's move ended.** Measured live
2026-08-11 on a wakeup Drive Parry set to a 1-frame input: the parry's own
animation runs 45 frames (12 minimum in the parry state, then a fixed 33 of
recovery), and `_State` was back at `READY` on frame **2** of it. The falling
edge marks the end of the *dispatch* — the recorded input finished playing —
which is exactly why the trial does not close there. See the settle phase
below.

### Only `_State` may begin a trial

One edge opens one — the dispatch (`_State` crossing onto the `PLAYING` side,
including a sampled 5 → 4 chain re-entry). One edge *arms* one — `_State`
entering `PLAY_WAIT`, where the identity (`RType`, `RndIndex`) is **latched**
for the dispatch to spend. Nothing else does either.

The latch/open split is forced by two measurements. Identity is only
trustworthy on the frame the reversal arms: the draw is fixed at the 2 → 3
edge, and `RndIndex` on other frames is re-roll garbage. And the dispatch
frame is where identity has been seen *lying*: measured live 2026-08-11,
`RType` flips `DOWN`(1) → `GUARD`(2) on the frame a wakeup Drive Parry enters
`PARRY`(39), with `_State` still on the playing side. (The machine once
compared `RType`/`RndIndex` every frame as a boundary signal; that charged the
session **two** trials for one reversal — visible in three archived sessions
as `down` / `guard` pairs where every `guard` row is one frame long and
carries `reversal_unresolved`.)

The latch is also what makes **aborts invisible by construction**: in the
guard group a blocked hit during `PLAY_WAIT` kicks the machine 3 → 2 without
dispatching (measured 2026-08-24), so a blockstring re-arms several times
before the reversal actually plays. Each abort merely drops or overwrites the
latch; only the arm that reaches the dispatch files a trial. A chain with no
observed `PLAY_WAIT` (a caught 5 → 4) has no latch to spend and falls back to
reading identity off the dispatch frame — best effort, for there is nowhere
better to read.

Known blind spot: a `Delay`-0 chain whose sub-frame `PLAYING` never survives
to a frame boundary reads as 5 → 5 and glues two reversals into one record.
Never observed.

### Which reversal fired

`_gData.RndIndex` names the winner of the game's random pick — but it counts
**the active entries of the group, not the configured 1-10 slot** (confirmed
live 2026-08-05: slots 1 and 7 active, slot 7 fires → `RndIndex` 1). The mod
recovers the configured slot at trial open by walking the group's ten entries,
keeping those with `IsActive`, and taking the `RndIndex`-th
([`infra/ReversalAccess.lua`](autorun/fgcnote/infra/ReversalAccess.lua)'s
`resolve_active_entry`).

Because that mapping depends on the **live** `IsActive` set, the witness here
backstops the identity, not just the contents: toggling reversals mid-session
shifts the mapping, the shifted entry's fields stop matching the spec's
witness, and the trial degrades to `spec_mismatch` — visibly — instead of
being graded against the wrong reversal's rules.

### The settle phase — how the trial ends

Both task types now use the same outcome-driven close predicate. A
slotResponse begins settling when recorded inputs end (§0/§4); a trigger
reversal begins settling when it returns to `READY`, because the punish the
task exists to grade can land **after** that edge.

This was a plain countdown until 2026-08-11 — `followFrames`, a per-reversal
number of frames to keep observing past the falling edge. It was replaced
because that number had to mean two things at once: the app's own help text
spelled it out as *"it must cover the dummy's recovery plus your response"*.
The recovery half is not something a task author should have to know per move,
and nothing in this project ever measured whether `READY` even **precedes** the
end of the dummy's recovery — the one experiment on record is a 20-frame
forward walk, and a walk has no recovery.

**The dummy's own action state ends the trial instead.** Past the falling edge
the mod reads `nBattle.cPlayer.act_st` on the dummy every frame and asks
[`lib/ActStCatalog.lua`](autorun/fgcnote/lib/ActStCatalog.lua)'s `is_settled`:

| class | meaning | effect on the trial |
|---|---|---|
| `own_action` | attacking, jumping, dashing, landing — busy with something of its own | keeps observing |
| `neutral` | grounded and free — it finished on its own | **closes** |
| `restrained` | hitstun, blockstun, knockdown — the player stopped it, and the hit is in | **closes** |
| `resolving` | `HOLD(38)` — caught in a throw or a super; the damage has not been applied yet | keeps observing |
| *unclassified* (`nil`) | this project has no classification for the id yet | keeps observing |

The whole rule is *"the trial ends the first frame the dummy's outcome is
decided"*. **There is no number** — a reversal entry carries no window length,
and the app has nothing to ask the user for.

**`resolving` is a bug fix, 2026-08-12.** `HOLD(38)` used to be plain
`restrained`, so a trial closed the instant the player's throw connected — and
a throw applies its damage 60 frames later on an ordinary throw, 481 on a
super (measured; `ActStCatalog`'s header lists the captures). Every punish
counter landed with a **throw** therefore scored zero. Not because throws are
unscoreable: because the window ended before the outcome existed to be
observed. The three archived 0-point trials all end on the single frame `p2`
enters `HOLD`, with the punish flag raised on that very frame.

**An unclassified id keeps the window open**, matching `ActStCatalog`'s rule
that `nil` is not a default and makes the mod do nothing. Eleven of the 44 ids
are still unclassified, `FALL(26)` among them, so that alone can keep a window
open indefinitely. `ReversalResponse.MAX_SETTLE_FRAMES` (900 frames past the
falling edge) closes it regardless — a real termination path, not a guard
against a bug.

That cap was 600 until the same change. Waiting through `resolving` makes it
reachable by a **real** state rather than only an unclassified one: a super's
`HOLD` is 481 frames of legitimate settling, and 600 would have closed some of
them mid-cinematic. A window the cap cuts off mid-throw comes back
`trial_truncated` (`Record.UNDECIDED_ACT_ST` includes `HOLD`) rather than
graded as a silent zero.

#### Why there is no trailing count

Between `followFrames` and this, the field was briefly `settleFrames` — the
same idea reduced to *"how many further frames to observe after the dummy
stops"*, `0..120`, default 30. Seven captured windows of one wakeup-DP drill
(2026-08-11) say what it bought: six were unchanged by it, and the seventh was
a hit landing **four frames after** the dummy had already returned to
`FOOTWORK`, which scored `damage` rather than `punish` — by then there was
nothing left to punish. Jaes's call: dropped, to be reinstated only if a real
drill needs it.

**The one-frame margin, stated plainly.** Closing on `restrained` means the
window ends on the frame the dummy enters `DAMAGE`, which is also the frame a
punish's flags arrive on. That frame **is** included: `Record:step` absorbs the
sample before the close is evaluated, and the one live capture of a 3-point
punish has `attr` and the punish flag on the same frame. If a capture ever
shows a flag arriving a frame late, the fix is to stop closing on `restrained`
and wait for `neutral` — not to reintroduce a countdown.

An **ignored** entry is the one trial that skips the settle phase entirely: it
has no answer to wait for, so it closes on the falling edge.

**The settle phase does not start until the falling edge.** Between the
dispatch and the fall the dummy is mid-move; the close condition is a question
that has not been asked yet. (During `PLAY_WAIT` no trial exists at all, so
the dummy standing in its `Delay` — which reads as `neutral` — can close
nothing.)

A new reversal starting during the settle phase closes the trial on the
previous frame and opens the next — the punish that knocked the dummy down
firing its down-reversal is the expected case, never a discard. The pause menu
during the settle phase **does** discard (unlike mid-reversal, where it forces
a falling edge that is then judged): nothing forces anything here, and letting
the window run on would grade a player who was reading a menu.

### The spec

```jsonc
{
    "schema": 1,
    "taskId": "wakeup-dp-drill",
    "type": "reversalResponse",
    "trialCount": 20,
    "characterName": "Ken",
    "reversals": [
        {
            "group": "down",             // "down" | "guard" | "damage"
            "slot": 3,                   // 1-10, the pause menu's numbering
            "label": "wakeup DP",        // echoed into trial records, for humans
                                         // no window length: the trial's end is
                                         //   read off the dummy's act_st (above)
            "witness": {                 // RAW config-entry field names -> expected
                "Type": 2,               //   values copied from listReversals'
                "SkillIndex": 5,         //   authoritative `fields` map
                "Level": 0
            },                           // At least one field.
            "rules": [                   // same vocabulary and first-match-wins
                { "when": "block",   "points": 2 },
                { "when": "got_hit", "points": -1 },
                { "when": "else",    "points": 0 }
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

The witness compares only the fields it names (its strength is the app's
choice, like the slot witness being a digest); a named field missing from the
live entry is a mismatch. `IsActive`/`IsValid` belong in no witness — activity
is live session state, the same rule the recording asset follows.

`"ignore": true` works here exactly as it does on a slot (§2) — a reversal that
is switched on for realism but is not what the drill grades. Same two rules: the
witness is still required and still checked first, `rules` must be absent, and a
spec whose every reversal is ignored is refused. It is also the one entry that
skips the settle phase: an ignored trial has no answer to wait for, so its
window closes on the reversal's own falling edge.

### The observation record

Identical shape, except the trial is addressed by `"group"` + `"slot"`
instead of `"slotId"` — both `null` when the identity never resolved:

| `diagnostic` | Meaning | Decided |
|---|---|---|
| `reversal_unresolved` | The runtime state named no reversal this mod could map back to a configured slot (group `NONE`, chain unreachable, `RndIndex` out of range) | trial opens |
| `no_spec_for_reversal` | The resolved group:slot has no entry in the spec | trial opens |
| `spec_mismatch` | The live entry's fields do not match the spec's witness — settings changed after the spec was authored, or the active-set shifted (above) | trial opens |
| `trial_truncated` | The dummy was still mid-attack on the closing frame | trial closes |

`trial_truncated` is the shared check in
[`func/Task/Record.lua`](autorun/fgcnote/func/Task/Record.lua) and is unchanged by the
settle phase. It rarely fires here now, because the settle phase closes on
`neutral`/`restrained` by construction: what is left is a filler entry closing
on the falling edge while the dummy is still recovering, a hand-off to the next
reversal, and a frame the Observer could not sample at all.

---

## 7. Compatibility

- `spec.schema` and the session document's `schema` version independently; both
  are 1. Bumped only for breaking shape changes; refuse a mismatch.
- The observation record gained `guardSt`/`counter`/`punish` on both contact
  lists and `dummyActionIds` on 2026-08-04 **without a schema bump**, which is
  the rule above being applied: an older reader ignores fields it does not know,
  and a newer reader must treat them as absent rather than required. Widening a
  record is not a breaking change; renaming or removing one would be.
- Unknown *fields* in a spec are ignored (forward compatibility); unknown
  *values* in closed sets — `when`, `type` — are refused (§2). The distinction
  is deliberate: an extra field is a newer app being polite, an unknown value
  is a disagreement about meaning.
- The spec gained `ignore` and the session document gained `ignored` on
  2026-08-07, again without a schema bump, by the same rule. Note which
  direction each degrades in: an older *reader* of a session ignores the new
  count, harmlessly; an older *mod* sent a spec containing an ignored entry
  refuses `startSession` outright with `slot N has no rules`, because rules
  used to be mandatory. That refusal is the wanted behaviour — the alternative
  would be a session silently grading the filler.
- `fgcnote/task/` is gitignored runtime state; `session.json` is safe to
  delete between sessions and regenerates on the next `startSession`.

我理解你的目標是：**保留現有計分能力，但把 Task Editor 從「設定底層規則」改成「描述這回合怎樣算好／壞」**。這次先討論，不改程式、不做 demo。

## 我確認到的現況

目前每個要練的行為都有自己的規則串，共 8 種條件：

- `damage`：你打中 dummy
- `counter`
- `punish`
- `block`：你擋下攻擊
- `got_hit`
- `thrown`
- `action`：你做出某個 Action ID
- `else`

規則是**由上往下檢查，第一個成立的就停止**。而且不同結果真的可能同時成立：

- 同一回合可以先擋下、後來又被打中。
- Counter／Punish／一般打中可能重疊。
- 指定動作可以和打中、被打中、防禦同時成立。

目前有幾個明顯的 UX 問題：

1. 八個條件全部平鋪在同一個 select，語意沒有分組。
2. `Action ID` 數字輸入仍是資料正本；「選招」只是幫忙把數字填進去。
3. `else` 可以被移到中間，導致後面的規則永遠不可能執行。
4. 選招時可以選玩家角色，但 Task 只保存數字，**沒有保存選的是哪個角色、哪招**。
5. 現在的編號與上下箭頭有表達順序，但還不像人在閱讀判斷邏輯。

## 我贊成你的四組，但名稱最好帶主詞

我會建議呈現成：

1. **我造成傷害**
   - 打中
   - Counter
   - Punish Counter
2. **我受到傷害**
   - 被打中
   - 被投
3. **我成功防禦**
   - 擋下
4. **我做出指定動作**
   - 直接選角色、招式與強度

「其他」不當成第五種條件，而是固定的最後結果。

分組應該放在「新增判定／選擇條件」裡，**不要把畫面切成四個獨立區塊**，因為四組之間仍然需要共同排序。

## Tree view：概念對，但我不建議做成真正的樹

目前資料模型沒有巢狀分支、AND／OR 或子條件，它其實是一條 `if / else if / else` chain。真正畫成 tree，會暗示使用者可以建立分支和巢狀邏輯。

我比較推薦做成有 tree 視覺的**判定鏈**：

```text
計分判定
由上往下，第一個成立的結果計分

如果       [我造成傷害 › Punish Counter]       +3
否則如果   [我做出指定動作 › Ryu 昇龍拳（重）] +2
否則如果   [我成功防禦 › 擋下]                 +1
否則如果   [我受到傷害 › 被打中]               -1
都沒有                                           0
```

可以保留左側直線、縮排和拖曳排序，但把「規則 1、2、3」換成「如果／否則如果／都沒有」。這樣使用者讀到的就是實際執行方式。

我也建議：

- 最後的「都沒有」固定在底部，不能移動。
- 指定動作顯示招式 chip，不顯示任何 Action ID。
- 單純條件不允許重複加入；指定動作則可以包含多招。
- 文案從「規則」改成「計分判定」或「怎樣算分」。

## Action ID 隱藏有一個現有資料問題

我同意 Action ID 不該出現在 UI。更完整的責任切法應是：

- Task 保存：玩家選的角色、招式、強度。
- App 在開始 run 時：把語意選擇解析成當前版本的 Action IDs。
- 傳給 mod 的 `TaskSpec`：仍然使用 Action IDs，現有協議不用改。

但目前已保存的 Task 只有 ID，未必能可靠反推出原本是哪招，尤其遇到舊版本、歧義或手動輸入的數字。因此之後要另外決定 legacy Task 怎麼處理。

## 我想先請你拍板三件事

1. 你說的「傷害／受傷」是**分組，底下仍保留細項**，還是要直接合併成粗粒度的一條？
   - 我推薦保留細項，否則會失去 Punish 比一般打中高分的能力。

2. 「都沒有」是否永遠固定存在，預設 0 分？
   - 我推薦是。這會直接移除一個難理解的狀態：沒配到任何規則但仍完成回合。

3. 指定動作出現時，是否接受整張 Task 增加一個「玩家使用角色」？
   - 我推薦接受，而且只在用了指定動作時要求。否則 Ryu 的昇龍拳條件在玩家改用 Ken 時，只會靜默永遠不成立。

**我的待驗證假設：玩家比較容易理解一條自然語言的判定鏈，而不是可展開的真正邏輯樹。** 這點要由你判斷是否符合你想要的操作感。

2跟3我都認同你的 然後我覺得我們先討論1 這樣才好討論判定鏈的問題 我想得是既可以粗粒度也可以細粒度（這樣的話 引用 AND 且邏輯進來 好像才是個好做法？）事實上的確有這個需求 會有一樣是做出指定ACTION ID 但最好是還有PUNISH COUNTER 如果沒懲罰反擊但有做出來就次佳 目前邏輯的判定也是寫在MOD那邊對不對？ 我會覺得改成比較複雜的邏輯設計會非常好 然後我在想這樣是不是把邏輯驗證放在APP會更好 可以實時的把關 使用者給的規則 會不會有邏輯上就永遠不會觸發的選項（例如先判定寬鬆的 再判定嚴格的） 嚴格的自然就永遠不會選到 或者我們可以自動優化成優先判定那些比較嚴格的 這種集合關係應該不難掌握

-- func/Task/Predicate.lua
-- Grades one observation record against a slot's app-authored rules, and
-- validates the whole task spec at startSession. Pure Lua, no REFramework
-- dependency: tools/smoke.lua runs all of it.
--
-- Also the module that owns the rule vocabulary -- TASK_PROTOCOL.md §2's table
-- and RULE_WHENS below must agree exactly, since an unrecognised `when` is
-- refused at startSession rather than allowed to quietly never match.
--
-- Everything read out of a contact is a FLAG MASK, tested with `&`, never
-- `==`: blocking a low arrives as grd|lo = 66, and `attr == 64` misses every
-- one (TASK_PROTOCOL.md §5). The masks stay behind the named helpers below so
-- no caller ever handles a bare constant.

local M = {}

-- nBattle.nHit.DMG_ATTR, complete, transcribed from the live dump at
-- fgcnote/devtools/data/enum/nBattle_nHit_DMG_ATTR.json (2026-08-04).
M.ATTR = {
    hi = 1, lo = 2, air = 4, all = 8, dis = 16,
    hit = 32, grd = 64, armor = 128, atemi = 256,
    parry = 512, d_grd = 1024, hit_catch = 2048, resv_dmg = 4096,
    blk_upp = 8192, blk_low = 16384, blk_air = 32768,
}

-- blk_upp|blk_low|blk_air -- the enum's own `blocking` composite (57344). Kept
-- out of the table above: anything iterating it as single bits would swallow
-- three real ones.
M.ATTR_BLOCKING = M.ATTR.blk_upp | M.ATTR.blk_low | M.ATTR.blk_air

-- nBattle.nHit.GUARD_ST, complete, from enum/nBattle_nHit_GUARD_ST.json. Three
-- groups share the field: the receiver's actual guard state, the attack's own
-- requirement (stand_ng/crouch_ng), and the dummy's configured behaviour (dmy_*).
-- info_set is a "this field is populated" marker and rides on every live sample.
M.GUARD_ST = {
    guard_self = 1, stand_ng = 2, crouch_ng = 4,
    guard_stand = 8, guard_crouch = 16, guard_air = 32,
    guard_auto = 256,
    dmy_guard_hi = 512, dmy_guard_mid = 1024, dmy_guard_low = 2048,
    dmy_parry = 4096, dmy_just = 8192,
    info_set = 32768,
}

--- The three actual-guard-state bits: "the receiver was guarding".
M.GUARDING = M.GUARD_ST.guard_stand | M.GUARD_ST.guard_crouch | M.GUARD_ST.guard_air

local function any(contacts, predicate)
    for _, contact in ipairs(contacts or {}) do
        if predicate(contact) then return true end
    end
    return false
end

local function mask(value)
    return tonumber(value) or 0
end

-- WAS THIS CONTACT BLOCKED?
--
-- guard_st decides, not dmg_attr. Confirmed live 2026-08-04: every blocked
-- contact arrived as attr = 1036 (air|all|d_grd) with `grd` CLEAR, so the
-- obvious `attr & grd` test never fired once and every blocked trial silently
-- fell through to `else`. guard_st said it outright on the same samples --
-- 32787 = info_set|guard_crouch|stand_ng|guard_self, i.e. a crouch block of
-- something that cannot be blocked standing -- and a contact the player did NOT
-- block came back with no guard bit at all (32768, info_set only).
--
-- The attr side is kept as an OR, not deleted: it costs nothing, it is what the
-- enum documents, and if some contact type reports the block only there, this
-- degrades to catching it rather than to missing it.
local function is_block(contact)
    return (mask(contact.guardSt) & M.GUARDING) ~= 0
        or (mask(contact.attr) & (M.ATTR.grd | M.ATTR.d_grd | M.ATTR_BLOCKING)) ~= 0
end

--- The derived booleans one record supports, computed once per grading.
--- Reads only fields the record carries -- never a live object, which by
--- resolve time has long reset (Observer.lua's header).
function M.summarize(record)
    record = type(record) == "table" and record or {}
    local dummy = record.dummyReceived
    local player = record.playerReceived
    return {
        damage = any(dummy, function(c) return (mask(c.attr) & M.ATTR.hit) ~= 0 end),
        counter = any(dummy, function(c) return c.counter == true end),
        punish = any(dummy, function(c) return c.punish == true end),
        block = any(player, is_block),
        got_hit = any(player, function(c) return (mask(c.attr) & M.ATTR.hit) ~= 0 end),
        -- A throw never sets dmg_attr (confirmed live 2026-08-05 -- see
        -- Record.lua's CATCH_ACT_ST), so it cannot be found in `player` above.
        -- CATCH is the THROWER's act_st, not the receiver's -- confirmed live
        -- 2026-08-05 the same session: three real dummy-throws-player trials
        -- all came back dummyCaught=true, playerCaught=false. "the player was
        -- thrown" therefore reads the dummy's latch, not the player's.
        thrown = record.dummyCaught == true,
    }
end

local function action_matches(rule, record)
    local seen = {}
    for _, id in ipairs(record.playerActionIds or {}) do seen[id] = true end
    for _, id in ipairs(rule.actionIds or {}) do
        if seen[tonumber(id)] then return true end
    end
    return false
end

--- First rule the record satisfies, in the order the app wrote them --
--- TASK_PROTOCOL.md §2's "first match wins", which is also the whole answer to
--- "does a punish also raise the counter flag": the app's ordering decides, so
--- the mod never has to know.
-- @return number? index (1-based), number? points, string? when -- all nil
--         when nothing matched (an app that wants a guaranteed match ends its
--         rules with `else`)
function M.evaluate(record, rules)
    local summary = M.summarize(record)
    for index, rule in ipairs(rules or {}) do
        local when = rule.when
        local matched
        if when == "else" then
            matched = true
        elseif when == "action" then
            matched = action_matches(rule, record)
        else
            matched = summary[when] == true
        end
        if matched then return index, tonumber(rule.points) or 0, when end
    end
    return nil, nil, nil
end

-- =========================================================
-- SPEC VALIDATION
-- =========================================================
-- Refusal messages name the failing field: they travel to result.json verbatim
-- and are the only debugging surface the app author gets.

M.RULE_WHENS = {
    damage = true, counter = true, punish = true,
    block = true, got_hit = true, thrown = true, action = true, ["else"] = true,
}

M.MIN_TRIALS, M.MAX_TRIALS = 1, 500

-- reversalResponse limits. Slots per group mirrors ReversalAccess
-- .SLOTS_PER_GROUP, restated here because this module stays REFramework-free
-- (tools/smoke.lua runs it) and cannot require the chain side.
--
-- A reversal entry carries NO window length. It used to (`followFrames`, then
-- `settleFrames`); the trial now ends when the dummy's own act_st says it
-- ended, which is not something a spec can state -- see ReversalResponse.lua's
-- header for what the number bought and why it was dropped.
M.REVERSAL_GROUPS = { down = true, guard = true, damage = true }
M.REVERSAL_SLOTS_PER_GROUP = 10

-- IGNORED ENTRIES -- the spec naming something on purpose without grading it.
--
-- A drill's random rotation usually has to contain behaviour that is not the
-- drill: a walk forward, a neutral pause, whatever keeps the dummy from being
-- a metronome. Those plays are real trials as far as the game is concerned,
-- and before this existed they arrived as no_spec_for_slot -- counted toward
-- trialCount, so a 20-trial session practised fifteen.
--
-- The declaration is EXPLICIT, never inferred from absence, and that is the
-- whole design. no_spec_for_slot is the only signal that surfaces a wrong
-- GAME_SLOT_BASE (TASK_PROTOCOL.md §4's "What the witness check does not
-- backstop"); a rule of "unmentioned means skip it" would trade the one
-- detector there is for silence, and the failure it detects looks exactly like
-- a session that scores nothing for no stated reason.
--
-- An ignored entry still carries a witness -- it is a slot the spec names, and
-- everything the spec names carries proof of what it thought was there -- and
-- must not carry rules, since rules on something never graded is a
-- contradiction rather than a preference.
local function validate_ignored(entry, where)
    if entry.rules == nil then return true end
    if type(entry.rules) == "table" and #entry.rules == 0 then return true end
    return false, where .. " is ignored but carries rules"
end

-- `where` is a caller-built label ("slot 3", "reversal down:2") because the
-- rule vocabulary is shared across task types and the message must still name
-- the failing spot in the spec's own terms.
local function validate_rules(rules, where)
    if type(rules) ~= "table" or #rules == 0 then
        return false, where .. " has no rules"
    end
    for index, rule in ipairs(rules) do
        local label = where .. " rule " .. index
        if type(rule) ~= "table" then return false, label .. " is not a table" end
        if not M.RULE_WHENS[rule.when] then
            return false, label .. " has unknown when: " .. tostring(rule.when)
        end
        if type(rule.points) ~= "number" then
            return false, label .. " has no numeric points"
        end
        if rule.when == "action" then
            if type(rule.actionIds) ~= "table" or #rule.actionIds == 0 then
                return false, label .. " (action) needs a non-empty actionIds"
            end
            for _, id in ipairs(rule.actionIds) do
                if type(id) ~= "number" then
                    return false, label .. " has a non-numeric action id"
                end
            end
        end
    end
    return true
end

local function validate_slot_entries(spec)
    if type(spec.slots) ~= "table" or #spec.slots == 0 then
        return false, "spec has no slots"
    end

    local seen = {}
    local gradable = 0
    for _, slot in ipairs(spec.slots) do
        if type(slot) ~= "table" then return false, "a slot entry is not a table" end
        local id = tonumber(slot.id)
        if not id or id < 1 or id > 8 or id ~= math.floor(id) then
            return false, "slot id must be 1-8, got " .. tostring(slot.id)
        end
        if seen[id] then return false, "slot " .. id .. " appears twice" end
        seen[id] = true

        -- Required of ignored entries too: a witness is what makes "this slot
        -- holds the filler I meant" checkable, so re-recording over the walk
        -- forward degrades to spec_mismatch instead of being skipped forever.
        local witness = slot.witness
        if type(witness) ~= "table"
            or not (tonumber(witness.frames) and tonumber(witness.frames) > 0)
            or type(witness.samples) ~= "string" or witness.samples == "" then
            return false, "slot " .. id .. " needs a witness with frames and samples"
        end

        local ok, err
        if slot.ignore == true then
            ok, err = validate_ignored(slot, "slot " .. id)
        else
            gradable = gradable + 1
            ok, err = validate_rules(slot.rules, "slot " .. id)
        end
        if not ok then return false, err end
    end

    -- An all-ignored spec would arm a session whose trial counter never moves:
    -- every play is dropped, trialsDone stays 0, and it runs until somebody
    -- stops it by hand. Refuse it where every other spec mistake is refused.
    if gradable == 0 then
        return false, "spec has no gradable slots: every slot is ignored"
    end
    return true
end

-- The reversal witness is a map of RAW config-entry field names (Type,
-- SkillIndex, Level, ...) to expected scalars -- the same names a snapshot's
-- `fields` map carries, so a spec is authored by copying out of one. Compared
-- key-by-key against the live entry at trial open
-- (func/Task/ReversalResponse.lua's witness_matches); which fields it pins
-- down is the app's choice, so the only shape rule is "at least one scalar".
local function validate_reversal_entries(spec)
    if type(spec.reversals) ~= "table" or #spec.reversals == 0 then
        return false, "spec has no reversals"
    end

    local seen = {}
    local gradable = 0
    for _, entry in ipairs(spec.reversals) do
        if type(entry) ~= "table" then return false, "a reversal entry is not a table" end
        if not M.REVERSAL_GROUPS[entry.group] then
            return false, "reversal group must be down/guard/damage, got " .. tostring(entry.group)
        end
        local slot = tonumber(entry.slot)
        if not slot or slot < 1 or slot > M.REVERSAL_SLOTS_PER_GROUP
            or slot ~= math.floor(slot) then
            return false, "reversal slot must be 1-" .. M.REVERSAL_SLOTS_PER_GROUP
                .. ", got " .. tostring(entry.slot)
        end
        local key = entry.group .. ":" .. slot
        if seen[key] then return false, "reversal " .. key .. " appears twice" end
        seen[key] = true

        -- Required of ignored entries too, for the same reason a slot's is:
        -- the witness is what makes the identity checkable, and here it also
        -- backstops the live-active-set mapping (TASK_PROTOCOL.md §6).
        if type(entry.witness) ~= "table" or next(entry.witness) == nil then
            return false, "reversal " .. key .. " needs a witness with at least one field"
        end
        for name, value in pairs(entry.witness) do
            local kind = type(value)
            if type(name) ~= "string"
                or (kind ~= "number" and kind ~= "boolean" and kind ~= "string") then
                return false, "reversal " .. key .. " witness field "
                    .. tostring(name) .. " is not a scalar"
            end
        end

        local ok, err
        if entry.ignore == true then
            ok, err = validate_ignored(entry, "reversal " .. key)
        else
            gradable = gradable + 1
            ok, err = validate_rules(entry.rules, "reversal " .. key)
        end
        if not ok then return false, err end
    end

    if gradable == 0 then
        return false, "spec has no gradable reversals: every reversal is ignored"
    end
    return true
end

--- Whole-spec shape check, run once at startSession. Unknown FIELDS pass
--- (forward compatibility); unknown VALUES in the closed sets are refused --
--- TASK_PROTOCOL.md §7 explains why the two are treated differently.
-- @return boolean ok, string? error
function M.validate_spec(spec)
    if type(spec) ~= "table" then return false, "no spec given" end
    if tonumber(spec.schema) ~= 1 then
        return false, "unsupported spec schema: " .. tostring(spec.schema)
    end
    if type(spec.taskId) ~= "string" or spec.taskId == "" then
        return false, "spec needs a taskId"
    end
    if type(spec.characterName) ~= "string" or spec.characterName == "" then
        return false, "spec needs a characterName"
    end
    local trials = tonumber(spec.trialCount)
    if not trials or trials < M.MIN_TRIALS or trials > M.MAX_TRIALS
        or trials ~= math.floor(trials) then
        return false, "trialCount must be an integer in " .. M.MIN_TRIALS .. ".." .. M.MAX_TRIALS
    end

    if spec.type == "slotResponse" then
        return validate_slot_entries(spec)
    elseif spec.type == "reversalResponse" then
        return validate_reversal_entries(spec)
    end
    return false, "unknown task type: " .. tostring(spec.type)
end

--- spec.slots re-keyed by slot id, the lookup every trial does.
function M.slots_by_id(spec)
    local by_id = {}
    for _, slot in ipairs(spec.slots or {}) do
        by_id[tonumber(slot.id)] = slot
    end
    return by_id
end

--- spec.reversals re-keyed by "group:slot", reversalResponse's equivalent.
function M.reversals_by_key(spec)
    local by_key = {}
    for _, entry in ipairs(spec.reversals or {}) do
        local slot = tonumber(entry.slot)
        if M.REVERSAL_GROUPS[entry.group] and slot then
            by_key[entry.group .. ":" .. slot] = entry
        end
    end
    return by_key
end

-- func/Task/Record.lua
-- Accumulates one trial's observation record from a stream of per-frame
-- samples (infra/CombatObserver.lua's shape). Pure Lua, no REFramework
-- dependency -- exercised by tools/smoke.lua with hand-built samples, the same
-- property SF6_TOOLS_CC's HitConfirm Engine has and the reason its grading
-- could be trusted without launching the game.
--
-- The one idea here is the CONTACT: a receiver's dmg_attr going nonzero opens
-- one, its return to zero closes it, and every flag seen in between is OR-ed
-- into the entry. Latching-by-OR is not decoration -- dmg_attr, guard_st and
-- the counter flags are all transient, and whether the game raises them on the
-- contact's first frame or a frame later is exactly the kind of micro-timing
-- this must not depend on. The cost is stated in TASK_PROTOCOL.md §3:
-- consecutive hits with no clean frame between them merge into one entry.
--
-- Record shape produced here = the observation record of TASK_PROTOCOL.md §3
-- MINUS the fields only the caller can know (trial number, label, diagnostic,
-- matchedRule, points).

local M = {}

-- The dummy still being in one of these act_st states when the window closed
-- means the window ended before the outcome was decidable -- the recording
-- convention of TASK_PROTOCOL.md §0, violated. Two families, one meaning:
--
--   * still ATTACKING: the recording ran out mid-move.
--   * still BEING THROWN: HOLD(38) is a waiting room, and the damage a throw
--     does is applied 60 to 481 frames after it starts (lib/ActStCatalog.lua's
--     `resolving` class, with the captures). A window closing here has watched
--     the throw connect and none of what it did.
--
-- HOLD was added 2026-08-12 alongside the fix that stops the settle phase
-- closing on it. It should now be unreachable through the normal close, which
-- is the point: the only ways left are MAX_SETTLE_FRAMES overrunning a super
-- and a hand-off to the next reversal, and both of those genuinely truncated
-- the trial. Reaching it is a signal, not noise.
--
-- 6 of nBattle.ACT_ST.ID's 44 values; the dump is
-- fgcnote/devtools/data/enum_nBattle_ACT_ST_ID.json. Renamed from ATTACKING_ACT_ST
-- when HOLD joined -- the old name would have been a lie about half the table.
M.UNDECIDED_ACT_ST = {
    [13] = true, -- ATCK_LAND
    [29] = true, -- ATCK
    [30] = true, -- SPECIAL
    [31] = true, -- SUPER
    [37] = true, -- CATCH
    [38] = true, -- HOLD
}

-- act_st is how a throw is detected, because dmg_attr is not known to move for
-- one: CATCH (nBattle.ACT_ST.ID 37, same enum UNDECIDED_ACT_ST reads above).
-- Confirmed live 2026-08-05 that this belongs to the THROWER, not the receiver
-- -- three zero-defense "throw loop" trials of the dummy throwing the player
-- came back dummyCaught=true, playerCaught=false every time (Predicate.lua's
-- `thrown` reads dummyCaught for exactly this reason). Latched like a flag,
-- not read once, for the same reason attr is OR-ed across a contact -- a
-- one-frame sampling gap must not un-catch someone.
--
-- THIS USED TO SAY "a throw never touches dmg_attr", on the evidence that
-- those three trials came back with playerReceived completely empty. WITHDRAWN
-- 2026-08-12: those windows closed on HOLD(38), and a throw's damage is
-- applied 60 to 481 frames later (lib/ActStCatalog.lua's `resolving`). The
-- trials measured a stretch of time the answer could not have been in.
-- Whether a throw sets dmg_attr at its DAMAGE frame is genuinely unmeasured,
-- and the window has to be reopened -- which the settle-phase fix does -- before
-- anyone can say. HOLD(38) is what the receiving side shows, which that same
-- comment listed as unknown.
M.CATCH_ACT_ST = 37

-- Bound on each side's action id list. Movement cycling through stances yields
-- maybe a dozen distinct ids per trial; a cap keeps a pathological trial from
-- growing a record without limit, and 32 is far above anything observed.
M.MAX_ACTION_IDS = 32

local Trial = {}
Trial.__index = Trial

--- Opens a trial at its rising edge.
-- @param start_frame number  GS.frame at the rising edge; contact `f`s and
--        the final `frames` are relative to it (TASK_PROTOCOL.md §3)
function M.begin(start_frame)
    return setmetatable({
        start_frame = tonumber(start_frame) or 0,
        -- Both sides carry the same fields, because Observer reads both sides
        -- the same way (its header explains why). A contact is a contact; which
        -- of them is interesting is a question for the rules, not for here.
        player_received = {},   -- { f, attr, guardSt, counter, punish }
        dummy_received = {},    -- same
        action_ids = {},
        dummy_action_ids = {},
        _action_seen = {},
        _dummy_action_seen = {},
        _p1_open = nil,         -- the entry currently being OR-ed into, or nil
        _p2_open = nil,
        player_caught = false,  -- p1 (receiver) ever seen in CATCH_ACT_ST
        dummy_caught = false,   -- p2, same
    }, Trial)
end

-- One side of one frame: extend the open contact or start one, and collect the
-- action id. Returns the open entry (or nil), which the caller holds onto.
local function absorb(side, open, contacts, rel, ids, seen)
    local attr = tonumber(side.attr) or 0
    if attr == 0 then
        open = nil
    else
        if not open then
            open = { f = rel, attr = 0, guardSt = 0, counter = false, punish = false }
            contacts[#contacts + 1] = open
        end
        -- OR, never assign: every flag is transient and the game may raise one
        -- a frame after the contact opened (module header).
        open.attr = open.attr | attr
        open.guardSt = open.guardSt | (tonumber(side.guard_st) or 0)
        open.counter = open.counter or side.counter == true
        open.punish = open.punish or side.punish == true
    end

    local id = tonumber(side.action_id) or -1
    if id >= 0 and not seen[id] and #ids < M.MAX_ACTION_IDS then
        seen[id] = true
        ids[#ids + 1] = id
    end

    return open
end

--- Feeds one frame. Safe to call with nil (a frame the Observer could not
--- sample) -- open contacts stay open rather than closing on a gap, because a
--- one-frame snapshot dropout mid-hitstop is not the contact ending.
function Trial:step(sample)
    if type(sample) ~= "table" then return end
    local rel = (tonumber(sample.frame) or 0) - self.start_frame

    if sample.p1 then
        self._p1_open = absorb(sample.p1, self._p1_open, self.player_received, rel,
            self.action_ids, self._action_seen)
        if tonumber(sample.p1.act_st) == M.CATCH_ACT_ST then self.player_caught = true end
    end

    if sample.p2 then
        self._p2_open = absorb(sample.p2, self._p2_open, self.dummy_received, rel,
            self.dummy_action_ids, self._dummy_action_seen)
        if tonumber(sample.p2.act_st) == M.CATCH_ACT_ST then self.dummy_caught = true end
    end
end

--- Closes the trial at its falling edge and hands back the record.
-- @param end_frame number  GS.frame at the falling edge
-- @param final_p2_act_st number?  the dummy's act_st on that frame, for the
--        truncation check; nil (unsampleable frame) counts as truncated,
--        because "could not prove the window was long enough" must not grade
--        as if it was
-- @return table record -- see module header for the shape
function Trial:finish(end_frame, final_p2_act_st)
    local act_st = tonumber(final_p2_act_st)
    return {
        frames = math.max(0, (tonumber(end_frame) or 0) - self.start_frame),
        playerReceived = self.player_received,
        dummyReceived = self.dummy_received,
        playerActionIds = self.action_ids,
        dummyActionIds = self.dummy_action_ids,
        playerCaught = self.player_caught,
        dummyCaught = self.dummy_caught,
        truncated = act_st == nil or M.UNDECIDED_ACT_ST[act_st] == true,
    }
end

return M

對，目前真正執行 run 時，**判定與計分是在 mod 裡完成的**：

- mod 的 `Predicate.lua` 把 observation 整理成 `damage / punish / block...` 布林值，再按照順序找第一條成立的規則。
- App 的 shared package 也有一份相同 evaluator，但目前主要用於測試與交叉驗證，renderer 實際上沒有拿它計分。
- App 現在只做 schema／欄位驗證，**不會檢查規則是否被前面的規則完全蓋住**。
- mod 在 `startSession` 時仍會再驗證一次 transport spec。

## AND 確實能表達你的案例

例如：

```text
如果［做出重昇龍］而且［Punish Counter］ → 3 分
否則如果［做出重昇龍］                 → 1 分
否則                                     → 0 分
```

第二條不需要明寫「而且沒有 Punish Counter」，因為第一條已經先攔截掉了。  
所以第一版其實只需要：

- 規則之間：`else if`
- 一條規則之內：`AND`
- 最後：固定 `else`

不一定要立刻開放任意的 `OR / NOT / 括號`。多招選擇本身可以是受控的 OR，例如「昇龍拳（輕／中／重任一）」。

資料概念可以改成：

```ts
{
  all: [
    { kind: 'action', move: ... },
    { kind: 'punish' }
  ],
  points: 3
}
```

App 保存使用者選的語意條件；開始 run 時再把招式轉成 Action IDs，編譯成 mod 可執行的 `TaskSpec`。

## App 很適合負責邏輯把關，但 mod 仍應負責執行

我建議責任這樣分：

### App

- 編輯語意規則。
- 即時分析規則。
- 找出重複、矛盾、永遠不會觸發的規則。
- 將較嚴格的規則正規化到較寬鬆規則前面。
- 把招式選擇解析成 Action IDs。
- 編譯成簡單、明確的 transport spec。

### Mod

- 防禦性驗證收到的 spec。
- 從遊戲逐幀產生 observation。
- 執行 App 編譯好的判定。
- 立即回傳 matched rule 和分數。

不建議把執行也完全移到 App，因為 mod 才握有逐幀狀態，也承擔即時遊戲回饋。比較好的方向是：**複雜的 authoring 與靜態分析在 App；簡單的 normalized evaluator 在 mod。**

## 集合關係可以自動處理，但只處理「可證明」的部分

例如：

```text
A AND B  ⊂  A
```

所以：

```text
做出重昇龍 AND Punish
```

必須排在：

```text
做出重昇龍
```

之前。這是數學上確定的，App 可以自動排序。

我會建議行為是：

- 使用者新增嚴格規則時，App 自動插到寬鬆規則前面。
- 畫面短暫說明：「已放在『做出重昇龍』之前，避免這條永遠無法觸發。」
- 已存在的錯誤順序直接標紅並阻止儲存，提供「修正順序」。
- 無法比較嚴格程度的規則，仍由使用者決定順序。例如「擋下」與「被打中」在同一 trial 可以同時成立，兩者沒有包含關係。
- 不根據分數高低排序；分數高不代表條件比較嚴格。

此外，可以偵測：

- 完全相同的兩條規則：第二條永遠不會觸發。
- `A` 在 `A AND B` 前：後者永遠不會觸發。
- 「不限強度昇龍」在「重昇龍」前：重昇龍規則被蓋住。
- 固定的 `else` 後面不允許任何規則。

但不能隨便假設 SF6 的領域關係。例如目前文件明確說「Punish 是否一定也會升起 Counter flag」尚未確認，因此 App 不能自行認定 `Punish ⊂ Counter`。如果要讓「細粒度是粗粒度子集合」成為可靠規則，我們應在 predicate 定義裡直接保證它，例如：

- 造成傷害：同一 contact 有 hit。
- Counter Hit：同一 contact 同時有 hit＋counter。
- Punish Counter：同一 contact 同時有 hit＋punish。

這樣 `Counter Hit ⊂ 造成傷害` 才是由我們的定義保證，而不是猜遊戲旗標關係。

## 但現在有一個必須先釐清的差異

目前 observation 保存的是：

- 整個 trial 做過哪些 Action IDs。
- 整個 trial 發生過哪些 contacts，以及哪些 contact 有 Punish flag。

它**沒有保存「是哪個 Action ID 造成哪個 contact」的關聯**。

所以這條：

```text
做出重昇龍 AND Punish Counter
```

以現在資料只能表示：

> 這個 trial 裡曾做出重昇龍，而且這個 trial 裡某次攻擊是 Punish Counter。

不能保證：

> 重昇龍本身打出了 Punish Counter。

如果 trial 裡先做了重昇龍，後來用另一招打出 Punish，現有 AND 也會成立。

我認為你的真正意圖比較可能是第二種：**指定的那一招本身產生了 Punish Counter**。若是這個意思，我們就不能只改規則 AST；還要讓 mod 在 contact 上保留攻擊方當時的 Action ID。技術上已有逐幀取樣點，但 Action ID 在 hitstop／contact 期間是否穩定，必須用實機證據驗證，不能直接假設。

所以我先只請你裁決這一題：

1. **Trial-level AND**：同一回合內兩件事都發生即可。
2. **Action-bound AND**：指定招式本身必須造成那個 Punish Counter。

我推薦 **2**。它更符合「有做出來是次佳，那一招成功懲罰才是最佳」的語意；只是會讓 observation contract 也進入這次設計範圍。
我覺得2是很合理 也不會說特別難做 做的fuzzy一點點 我也認為無傷大雅 不過有個點我好奇你怎麼想 mod可以單純的把per frame的資料給app main process 讓app自己處理會不會更好阿 也不會佔用遊戲資源？ 我直覺上會覺得把判定放在mod沒有什麼好處 統一在一個地方處理也很好 也還不用特別編譯過去？

-- =========================================================
-- PER-FRAME
-- =========================================================

local function handle_event(s, event)
    if event.discarded then
        s.discarded = s.discarded + 1
        M.status.discarded = s.discarded
        publish(s, "running", nil)
        return
    end

    -- Filler the spec declared: counted so the user can see how much of the
    -- rotation is scenery, and otherwise inert -- no observation record, no
    -- trial number, nothing toward trialCount. The count is deliberately not a
    -- trials[] entry: §0's "persist observations" is about answers, and this
    -- was never one.
    if event.ignored then
        s.ignored = s.ignored + 1
        M.status.ignored = s.ignored
        publish(s, "running", nil)
        return
    end

    -- The two task types address a trial differently and the record says so:
    -- slotId for slotResponse, group+slot for reversalResponse (nil when the
    -- identity never resolved -- TASK_PROTOCOL.md §6).
    local trial = event.record
    local spec_entry
    if s.kind == "reversalResponse" then
        trial.group = event.group
        trial.slot = event.slot
        spec_entry = event.group and event.slot
            and s.lookup[event.group .. ":" .. event.slot] or nil
    else
        trial.slotId = event.slotId
        spec_entry = s.lookup[event.slotId]
    end
    trial.trial = #s.trials + 1
    trial.label = spec_entry and spec_entry.label or nil
    trial.diagnostic = event.diagnostic
    -- `truncated` was folded into `diagnostic`; the record does not carry the
    -- same fact twice.
    trial.truncated = nil

    if not event.diagnostic and spec_entry then
        local index, points = Predicate.evaluate(trial, spec_entry.rules)
        trial.matchedRule = index
        trial.points = points
        s.total_points = s.total_points + (points or 0)
    end

    s.trials[#s.trials + 1] = trial
    M.status.trials_done = #s.trials
    M.status.total_points = s.total_points

    if #s.trials >= s.spec.trialCount then
        end_session("finished", nil)
    else
        publish(s, "running", nil)
    end
end

--- Call once per rendered frame, AFTER GameState's updater has run. Costs one
--- boolean check while no session is running.
function M.tick()
    local s = session
    if not s then return end

    -- Losing the prerequisite mid-run cannot silently fall back to the old
    -- recording-edge window: the next slot could begin while this one is still
    -- settling and contaminate both observations. Stop loudly instead.
    if s.kind == "slotResponse" and not Features.active("smartplayback") then
        end_session("stopped", "SmartPlayback disabled during session")
        return
    end

    -- Training mode lost mid-session: stop BEFORE stepping the machine. The
    -- exit also drops is_replaying, and stepping first would let that bogus
    -- falling edge resolve as a real trial.
    if not Access.is_training_mode() then
        end_session("stopped", "left training mode")
        return
    end

    local event = s.machine:step(Observer.read(_G.fgcnote_GameState))
    if event then handle_event(s, event) end
end

return M

-- infra/CombatObserver.lua
-- One read-only frame of both fighters' raw execution/contact state.
--
-- Promoted from func/Task/Observer.lua when Timeline execution observations
-- became the second shipping consumer. Task still uses the compact contact
-- fields it always did; actiontrace also preserves the measured M1 candidate
-- fields needed to determine external hit/guard/parry/throw/interruption in
-- the app. No validity or move semantics live here.
--
-- Contact fields are receiver-centric: p1 describes what reached P1 and p2
-- what reached P2. The game facts and current-build evidence are in
-- docs/kb/execution-observations.md.

require("fgcnote/infra/SharedHooks")

local M = {}

local FIELD_KINDS = {
    attr = { game = "dmg_attr", kind = "number", fallback = 0 },
    guard_st = { game = "guard_st", kind = "number", fallback = 0 },
    counter = { game = "counter_dm_flag", kind = "boolean", fallback = false },
    punish = { game = "counter_fw_flag", kind = "boolean", fallback = false },
    catch_flag = { game = "catch_flag", kind = "boolean" },
    damage_time = { game = "damage_time", kind = "number" },
    damage_sleep = { game = "damage_sleep", kind = "number" },
    damage_back = { game = "damage_back", kind = "number" },
    damage_type = { game = "damage_type", kind = "number" },
    vital_new = { game = "vital_new", kind = "number" },
}

local descriptors = nil

local function resolve_fields(player)
    local td = player:get_type_definition()
    local out = {}
    for name, spec in pairs(FIELD_KINDS) do out[name] = td:get_field(spec.game) end
    descriptors = out
end

local function number(value)
    return tonumber(value) or tonumber(tostring(value))
end

local function read_field(player, name, spec)
    local field = descriptors and descriptors[name]
    if not field then return spec.fallback end
    local ok, value = pcall(function() return field:get_data(player) end)
    if not ok or value == nil then return spec.fallback end
    if spec.kind == "boolean" then return value == true end
    return number(value) or spec.fallback
end

local function action_engine(player)
    local engine = nil
    pcall(function()
        local action_param = player and player.mpActParam
        local action_part = action_param and action_param.ActionPart
        engine = action_part and action_part._Engine
    end)
    return engine
end

local function call_number(engine, method)
    if not engine then return nil end
    local ok, value = pcall(function() return engine:call(method) end)
    return ok and number(value) or nil
end

local function read_side(player, act_st)
    local side = { act_st = tonumber(act_st) or 0 }
    for name, spec in pairs(FIELD_KINDS) do side[name] = read_field(player, name, spec) end

    local engine = action_engine(player)
    side.action_id = call_number(engine, "get_ActionID") or -1
    side.action_frame = call_number(engine, "get_ActionFrameNum")
    side.base_style = call_number(engine, "get_BaseStyleIndex")
    side.locked_style = call_number(engine, "get_LockedStyleIndex")
    return side
end

--- @param gs table? injected GameState-compatible snapshot
--- @return table? { frame, p1 = <raw side>, p2 = <raw side> }
function M.read(gs)
    if not gs or not gs.valid or not gs.p1 or not gs.p2 then return nil end
    if not descriptors then
        local ok = pcall(resolve_fields, gs.p1)
        if not ok or not descriptors then return nil end
    end
    return {
        frame = gs.frame,
        p1 = read_side(gs.p1, gs.p1_act_st),
        p2 = read_side(gs.p2, gs.p2_act_st),
    }
end

return M
